**Step 1: Find angle R in triangle PQR.**

The angles of a triangle sum to 180°:
$$\angle R = 180° - \angle P - \angle Q = 180° - 40° - 35° = 105°$$

**Step 2: Use the parallel lines.**

Points S and T lie on segments PQ and PR respectively, with ST ∥ QR. Line PR acts as a transversal cutting the parallel lines ST and QR.

- Ray TS is parallel to ray RQ (same direction).
- Ray TR (from T toward R) points opposite to ray RP (from R toward P), since T lies between P and R.

Therefore ∠STR and ∠QRP (= ∠R) are same-side (consecutive) interior angles, so they are supplementary:
$$\angle STR = 180° - \angle R = 180° - 105° = 75°$$

\boxed{75}

- Q = (0,0)
- R = (1,0)
- P = (1.1, 0.5)
- SS = 0.6*P = (0.66, 0.3) — this is point S
- T = R + 0.6*(P-R) = (1,0) + 0.6*(0.1, 0.5) = (1,0) + (0.06, 0.3) = (1.06, 0.3) — this is point T

The drawing is: T--SS--P--R--Q--SS

So the segments drawn are:
- T to S
- S to P
- P to R
- R to Q
- Q to S

- Triangle PQR with vertices P, Q, R
- S is a point on segment PQ (since SS = 0.6*P, and Q is at origin, so S is on QP)
- T is a point on segment PR (since T = R + 0.6*(P-R), T is on RP)

T = R + 0.6*(P-R). This is a point on segment RP, at 60% of the way from R to P. So T is on segment RP.

The segments drawn: T--S (segment TS), S--P (segment SP), P--R (segment PR), R--Q (segment RQ), Q--S (segment QS).

So we have triangle PQR, with S on PQ and T on PR, and segment ST drawn.

At point R, the angle between RQ and RP is angle R = 105° (angle PRQ).

At point T, the angle between TS and TR: since ST ∥ QR, and PR is the transversal...

The angle STR and angle QRP (which is angle R = 105°) — let me think about whether they're corresponding, alternate interior, etc.

T is on segment PR, between P and R. S is on segment PQ, between P and Q.

ST ∥ QR.

The transversal is line PR. At point T, the line ST goes from T toward S (which is toward the PQ side). At point R, the line QR goes from R toward Q.

Since ST ∥ QR, and both S and Q are on the same side of line PR (the left side), the angles that ST and QR make with the transversal PR at T and R respectively are corresponding angles.

Angle STR is the angle at T between ray TS and ray TR. Ray TR points from T toward R (downward along PR). Ray TS points from T toward S.

Angle QRP is the angle at R between ray RQ and ray RP. Ray RP points from R toward P (upward along PR). Ray RQ points from R toward Q.

Hmm, let me set up coordinates to be sure.

Q = (0,0), R = (1,0), P = (1.1, 0.5).
S = (0.66, 0.3), T = (1.06, 0.3).

Vector TS = S - T = (0.66 - 1.06, 0.3 - 0.3) = (-0.4, 0). So TS points in direction (-1, 0), i.e., straight left.

Vector TR = R - T = (1 - 1.06, 0 - 0.3) = (-0.06, -0.3). 

Angle STR is the angle between vectors TS and TR at vertex T.

cos(angle) = (TS · TR)/(|TS||TR|) = ((-0.4)(-0.06) + (0)(-0.3))/(|TS||TR|) = (0.024 + 0)/(|TS||TR|) = 0.024/(0.4 × √(0.0036+0.09)) = 0.024/(0.4 × √0.0936) = 0.024/(0.4 × 0.306) = 0.024/0.1224 ≈ 0.196.

angle ≈ 78.7°.

Let me redo with the actual angle constraints.

Angle R = 180 - 40 - 35 = 105°.

Now ST ∥ QR. The angle STR: at vertex T, between ray TS and ray TR.

Since ST ∥ QR, ray TS is parallel to ray RQ (both point in the same direction? Let's check: TS direction is from T to S, RQ direction is from R to Q).

In the coordinate example: TS = (-0.4, 0), RQ = Q - R = (-1, 0). Yes, same direction.

Ray TR is from T to R, along line PR, pointing toward R. Ray RP is from R to P, pointing toward P. These are opposite directions along the same line.

So angle STR (between TS and TR) and angle QRP... wait, angle at R between RQ and RP.

Angle QRP is between ray RQ and ray RP. Ray RQ = (-1,0) direction, ray RP = P - R = (0.1, 0.5) direction.

Angle STR is between ray TS = (-1,0) direction and ray TR = R - T direction = toward R = (-0.06, -0.3) which is opposite to RP direction.

So angle STR = angle between (-1,0) and (-RP direction) = 180° - angle between (-1,0) and (RP direction) = 180° - angle QRP = 180° - 105° = 75°.

Let me verify: angle between (-1,0) and (0.1, 0.5): cos = (-0.1)/(1 × √(0.01+0.25)) = -0.1/0.5099 = -0.196, angle ≈ 101.3°. Hmm that doesn't equal 105° because the coordinates don't match the given angles. But the relationship angle STR = 180° - angle R holds.

So angle STR = 180° - 105° = 75°.

Let me double check the reasoning: ST ∥ QR means ray TS ∥ ray RQ (same direction). The transversal line PR: at T, ray TR points one way; at R, ray RP points the opposite way (since T is between P and R, ray TR from T goes toward R, ray RP from R goes toward P, opposite). 

So angle STR and angle QRP are supplementary (consecutive interior angles / same-side interior angles with the parallel lines and transversal). Hence angle STR = 180° - 105° = 75°.

Thus the answer is 75°.

Let me confirm angle R = 105°: 40 + 35 + 105 = 180. Yes.

Answer: 75.
